Description: The technique used to reprogram source cells into pluripotent stem cells or directly into another cell type.
Valid Values: adenoviral vectors, chemical reprogramming, episomal vectors, lentiviral transduction, microRNA-based reprogramming, minicircle vectors, mRNA transfection, piggyBac transposon, protein transduction, retroviral transduction, Sendai virus

Description: Transient transfection method involving the transgene introduction into the cells of interest using engineered adenoviral particles. Adenoviral particles can transduce both replicating and non-dividing cells. Adenoviral DNA does not integrate into the host genome, but rather, resides episomally in the host nucleus.
Reprogramming of cells using small-molecule compounds alone, without introducing exogenous genes, RNA or proteins.

Reprogramming by transfection with non-integrating episomal plasmid vectors, typically oriP/EBNA1-based, which are maintained extrachromosomally and are gradually lost from the culture as the cells divide.
Stable transfection method involving the transgene introduction into the cells of interest using engineered lentiviral particles.
Reprogramming induced by introducing microRNAs (e.g. the miR-302/367 cluster) into cells, alone or together with other reprogramming factors.
Non-integrating circular DNA vectors that lack bacterial plasmid backbone sequences, used to transiently express reprogramming factors.
Reprogramming by repeated transfection of synthetic modified messenger RNA encoding the reprogramming factors. The mRNA is translated transiently and degraded, so no DNA is introduced into the cell.

Reprogramming by transfection with a piggyBac transposon carrying the reprogramming factors. The transposon integrates at TTAA sites and can subsequently be excised by piggyBac transposase, allowing the factors to be removed from the genome without leaving a residual footprint.
Delivery of recombinant reprogramming factor proteins, typically fused to a cell-penetrating peptide, into cells without introducing nucleic acids.
Stable transfection method involving the transgene introduction into the cells of interest using engineered retroviral particles.

Reprogramming by transduction with a non-integrating Sendai virus vector. Sendai virus is a negative-sense RNA virus that replicates in the cytoplasm, so the reprogramming factors are expressed without entering the host genome, and the vector is progressively diluted out of the culture with successive passages.
